content: The term Big Tobacco is a derogatory label commonly used to describe the tobacco industry as a whole, or more specifically, the three largest tobacco corporations in the United States. These corporations are Philip Morris (also known as Altria), R.J. Reynolds (RJR), and British American Tobacco. The term is frequently employed in anti-smoking campaigns, such as those by TheTruth.com and the Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids, which are initiatives funded by the Master Settlement Agreement. Occasionally, the term may also encompass other significant players in the tobacco market, such as Lorillard or Brown & Williamson. In popular culture, Big Tobacco has been used as a satirical reference. For instance, in the comic movie Mystery Men, one of the villains, who leads a gang with a business-oriented theme and is often seen smoking cigars, adopts the alias Big Tobacco. Similarly, the movie Thank You for Smoking features a character named Nick Naylor, portrayed by Aaron Eckhart, who works as a lobbyist for the tobacco industry. In the film, the influence and tactics of Big Tobacco are highlighted, including a quote that humorously underscores the industry's efforts to maintain smoking addiction: Big Tobacco didn't spend billions of dollars making it impossible to quit smoking so that anyone with a hammer, an ice pick, and good aim could make it any easier, as stated by Stephen Colbert.
